'''Gloria Conyers Hewitt''' (born October 26, 1935) is an American mathematician. She was the fourth African-American woman to receive a Ph.D. in mathematics.<ref name="NWM"/><ref>According to Kenschaft: ''Change Is Possible: Stories of Women and Minorities in Mathematics,'' [[American Mathematical Society]], 2005, p. 5, she has been the fifth.</ref> Her main research interests were in [[group theory]] and [[abstract algebra]]. She is the first African American woman to chair a math department in the United States.

==Early life and education==
Hewitt was born on October 26, 1935, in [[Sumter, South Carolina|Sumter]], [[South Carolina]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Black Women in America: An Historical Encyclopedia|year=1994|publisher=Indiana University Press|location=Bloomington|isbn=978-0-253-32774-1|chapter=Hewitt, Gloria Conyers (1935–)|pages=557–558|first=Patricia Clark|last=Kenschaft|author-link=Patricia Clark Kenschaft}}</ref> She entered [[Fisk University]] in 1952 and graduated in 1956 with a degree in secondary mathematics education. Without her knowledge, department chairman [[Lee Lorch]] recommended Hewitt to two graduate schools. As a result, she was offered a fellowship at the [[University of Washington]] in her senior year, though she had not applied for it.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.agnesscott.edu/lriddle/women/hewitt.htm|title=Gloria Hewitt|website=www.agnesscott.edu|access-date=2016-11-29}}</ref> Hewitt received her master's degree from there in 1960, and then her Ph.D. (with a thesis on "Direct and Inverse Limits of Abstract Algebras") in 1962.<ref name="NWM">Charlene Morrow and Teri Perl (eds), ''Notable Women in Mathematics'', Greenwood Press, 1998, pp. 76–79.</ref><ref name=":0" />

==Career==
In 1961, Hewitt joined the faculty at the [[University of Montana]].<ref name=":0" /> In 1966 she became tenured and promoted to associate professor, then in 1972, to full professor.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Lattimore|first=Randy|year=2001|title=Gloria Hewitt: Mathematician|url=https://rhsmathdepartment.wikispaces.com/file/view/Gloria+Hewitt.pdf|publisher=The National Council of Teachers of Mathematics|volume=94|pages=|via=|access-date=2016-11-29|archive-date=2020-08-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200822154409/https://rhsmathdepartment.wikispaces.com/file/view/Gloria+Hewitt.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1995, she was elected chair of the Department of Mathematical Science.<ref name="NWM"/> She served in that position until she retired in June 1999, with the title of [[Professor Emeritus]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

While a professor at the University of Montana she participated in multiple other organizations. She served on the executive council of the mathematical honor society, [[Pi Mu Epsilon]].<ref name=":1" /> She served as the chair of the committee that writes questions for the mathematics section of the [[Graduate Record Examinations|GREs]].<ref name=":1" /> Hewitt was also a faculty consultant for the [[Advanced Placement]] examination in calculus.<ref name=":1" /> In 1995, she was awarded an ETS Certificate of Appreciation after twelve years of service.<ref name=":1" />

Hewitt served on the Board of Governors of the Mathematical Association of America.<ref name="Gloria Hewitt">{{Cite web|url=https://www.agnesscott.edu/lriddle/women/hewitt.htm|title=Gloria Hewitt|website=www.agnesscott.edu|access-date=2018-10-06}}</ref>

She was known for many mathematics accomplishments but most of all for being one of the first three black women to receive a mathematics award.

Hewitt's works focus on two mathematic areas: abstract algebra and group theory.<ref name=":1" /> She has eight published research papers and twenty-one unpublished lectures.<ref name=":1" />

One would expect Hewitt to have faced many racial and gender oriented obstacles; however, in a personal interview she stated that she did not feel there had been any racial incidents in her career that had a detrimental effect on her studies.<ref name=":0" /> She did however, write an article in the ''[[Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences]]'', titled "The Status of Women in Mathematics".<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hewitt|first=Gloria C.|date=1979-04-01|title=The Status of Women in Mathematics|journal=Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=323|issue=1|pages=100–109|doi=10.1111/j.1749-6632.1979.tb16844.x|bibcode=1979NYASA.323..100H|s2cid=83866914|issn=1749-6632}}</ref>   Hewitt has said that "Some of my fellow graduate students did all they could to help and encourage me.  They included me in most of their activities.  I know this situation was not the norm for a lot of Blacks studying mathematics, but I was fortunate enough to be at the right place at the right time."<ref name="Gloria Hewitt"/>

==Awards and recognition==
She was awarded a prestigious [[National Science Foundation]] postdoctoral Science Faculty [[Scholarship|Fellowship]].  She was elected to the board of governors of the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref name="NWM"/> Her accomplishments have also earned her recognition by [[Mathematically Gifted & Black]] as a Black History Month 2018 Honoree.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Gloria Conyers Hewitt|url=https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/honorees/gloria-conyers-hewitt/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=Mathematically Gifted & Black}}</ref> In 2018, the University of Washington established the [https://math.washington.edu/news/2018/04/03/gloria-hewitt-graduate-support-fund-established Gloria Hewitt Endowed Graduate Student Support Fund] in honor of Hewitt's immense contributions to the field of mathematics. The fund, established with an initial principal amount of $50,000, was set up to "promote excellence in the graduate program of the Department of Mathematics, in particular enhancing efforts to achieve a more equitable representation of those under-represented in the field of mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gloria Hewitt Graduate Support Fund established {{!}} Department of Mathematics {{!}} University of Washington |url=https://math.washington.edu/news/2018/04/03/gloria-hewitt-graduate-support-fund-established |access-date=2023-01-04 |website=math.washington.edu}}</ref>
